title: The Inverse Function Theorem will tell us the slope of the tangent line to the Inverse function.
text: The Inverse Function Theorem is $$g'(x)=\frac{1}{h{\left(g{\left(x\right)}\right)}}$$ where g(x) is the inverse of f(x) and $$h(x)=f'(x)$$ or in other words h(x) is the derivative of f(x).

title: Finding the Inverse of f(x) at $$a=16$$.
text: To find the inverse of f(x) where $$a=16$$ (remember that a is equal to the x-value of a point), then we need to first find what value of $$x$$ when we plug it into f(x) will give us a value of $$16$$. In this case, it is when $$x=1$$, so we know that $$g(16)=1$$ where g(x) is the inverse of f(x).

title: Finding the Derivative of f(x)
text: Next, to find the derivative of f(x), use the power rule together with the chain rule: multiply by the exponent $$4$$, subtract $$1$$ from the exponent, and multiply by the derivative of $$x^3+1$$, which is $$3x^2$$.

title: Applying the Inverse Function Theorem
text: Since we already found $$g(16)=1$$ (remember g(x) is the inverse of f(x)) and the derivative of f(x) (h(x)), then we can plug what we know into the inverse function theorem. Our resulting slope is $$\frac{1}{96}$$.
